source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 15 (i)-(iv): show four integrals are zero (Properties IV, V); book pp. 102-103. No printed answer (show that).

blocks.explanation:
Yeh 'saabit karo ke zero hai' wala sawal hai. \(\ln(\tan x)\) ka antiderivative aasaan nahi, is liye property se kaam lenge.
Diya kya hai? Limits \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), jin ka jama \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hai.
Kya saabit karna hai? Integral 0 hai.
Rule kaunsa? Property IV: \(x\) ki jagah \(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\). Is se \(\tan x\) ban jata hai \(\cot x\), aur \(\ln \cot x = -\ln \tan x\). To integral apne negative ke barabar aayega.
Plan: Property IV, log ka qanoon, \(I = -I\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \ln(\tan x)\,dx\).
Saabit karna: \(I = 0\).
Tareeqa: Property IV, jahan \(a + b - x = \frac{\pi}{2} - x\), aur identity \(\tan(\frac{\pi}{2} - x) = \cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x}\). Is poore sawal ki 'replace aur jama/compare' wali chaal yahi hai.

Property IV lagayein
\[I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \ln\left(\tan\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)\right)dx\]
\[= \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\tan x}\right)dx\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2}\), to \(x\) ki jagah \(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\). Complementary angle ka tan, cot hota hai: \(\tan(\frac{\pi}{2} - x) = \cot x\).

Log ka qanoon
\[\ln\dfrac{1}{\tan x} = -\ln(\tan x)\]
\[I = -\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \ln(\tan x)\,dx = -I\]
Kyun: \(\ln\frac{1}{p} = \ln 1 - \ln p = -\ln p\). Is interval par \(\tan x\) positive hai, to log ki value bani rehti hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\ln\frac{1}{\tan x}\) ko \(\frac{1}{\ln \tan x}\) samajhna bari ghalti hai.

Nateeja
\[I = -I \Rightarrow 2I = 0 \Rightarrow I = 0\]
Kyun: jo number apne negative ke barabar ho woh 0 hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\ln \tan\tfrac{\pi}{6} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\ln 3,\quad \ln \tan\tfrac{\pi}{3} = +\tfrac{1}{2}\ln 3\]
Kyun: graph left aadhe mein negative aur right aadhe mein utna hi positive hai (aaine wale points \(x\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\) par values ulti hain); dono areas cancel. Calculator bhi 0 deta hai.

blocks.prompt: 15 (ii) Show that: \(\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x \cos x}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\,dx = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi 'zero saabit karo' wala sawal hai; limits ka jama \(0 + \pi = \pi\).
Diya kya hai? Integrand mein \(\sin x\), \(\cos x\) aur \(e^{\sin x}\).
Kya saabit karna hai? Integral 0 hai.
Rule kaunsa? Property IV: \(x\) ki jagah \(\pi - x\). Is se \(\sin x\) wohi rehta hai lekin \(\cos x\) ka sign ulat jata hai. Neeche sirf \(\sin x\) hai, to woh nahi badalta; poora integrand ulta ho jata hai.
Plan: Property IV, compare, \(I = -I\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x \cos x}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\,dx\).
Saabit karna: \(I = 0\).
Tareeqa: Property IV \(x \to \pi - x\), aur identities \(\sin(\pi - x) = \sin x\), \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\).

Property IV lagayein
\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin(\pi - x)\cos(\pi - x)}{1 + e^{\sin(\pi - x)}}\,dx\]
\[= \int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin x\,(-\cos x)}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\,dx\]
Kyun: second quadrant mein sine positive rehta hai aur cosine negative ho jata hai; isi liye \(\sin(\pi - x) = \sin x\) aur \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\). Denominator mein sirf \(\sin x\) hai, to woh bilkul nahi badla.

Muqabla karein
\[I = -\int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\,dx = -I\]
Kyun: minus bahar nikala; jo bacha woh asal \(I\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(e^{\sin(\pi - x)}\) ko \(e^{-\sin x}\) likhna ghalat hai; sine ka sign nahi badalta.

Nateeja
\[2I = 0 \Rightarrow I = 0\]
Kyun: \(I = -I\) sirf 0 ke liye sach hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{4}:\ \cos x > 0;\quad x = \tfrac{3\pi}{4}:\ \cos x < 0\]
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke ird gird aaine wale points par integrand ki values barabar magar ulti hain, to areas cancel ho jate hain. Calculator bhi 0 deta hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{\sin x \cos x}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\,dx = 0\).

blocks.explanation:
Is mein bhi limits ka jama \(\pi\) hai.
Diya kya hai? Integrand teen hisson ka product: \(x\), \((\pi - x)\) aur \(\cos(\pi - x)\).
Kya saabit karna hai? Integral 0 hai.
Rule kaunsa? Property IV (\(x \to \pi - x\)). \(x(\pi - x)\) wala hissa wohi rehta hai (do factors aapas mein jagah badal lete hain), lekin cosine wala hissa ulta ho jata hai. To \(I = -I\).
By parts se bhi ho sakta hai, lekin property wala raasta bohat chhota hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x(\pi - x)\cos(\pi - x)\,dx\).
Saabit karna: \(I = 0\).
Tareeqa: Property IV, \(x \to \pi - x\).

Property IV lagayein
\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x)\big(\pi - (\pi - x)\big)\cos\big(\pi - (\pi - x)\big)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x)\,x\,\cos x\,dx\]
Kyun: har jagah \(x\) ki jagah \(\pi - x\) rakha; \(\pi - (\pi - x) = x\). Pehle do factors ne bas jagah badli: \(x(\pi - x)\) ban gaya \((\pi - x)x\), jo wohi hai.
Dhyan dein: har \(x\) ko badalna hai, sirf cosine ke andar wale ko nahi.

Asal se muqabla karein
\[\cos x = -\cos(\pi - x)\]
\[I = -\int_{0}^{\pi} x(\pi - x)\cos(\pi - x)\,dx = -I\]
Kyun: \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\), to ulta bhi sach hai: \(\cos x = -\cos(\pi - x)\). Rakhne par asal integrand ka minus aaya.

Nateeja
\[2I = 0 \Rightarrow I = 0\]
Kyun: \(I = -I\).

Tasdeeq: by parts se
\[I = -\int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi x - x^2)\cos x\,dx\]
\[\int_{0}^{\pi} \pi x\cos x\,dx = -2\pi,\quad \int_{0}^{\pi} x^2\cos x\,dx = -2\pi\]
Kyun: \(\int x\cos x\,dx = x\sin x + \cos x\) se pehla \(\pi(-1 - 1) = -2\pi\); \(\int x^2\cos x\,dx = x^2\sin x + 2x\cos x - 2\sin x\) se doosra \(2\pi(-1) = -2\pi\). To \(I = -(-2\pi + 2\pi) = 0\). Dono raaste ek hi jawab dete hain.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi} x(\pi - x)\cos(\pi - x)\,dx = 0\).

blocks.explanation:
Ghaur karein: integrand mein har jagah \(x - 2\) hai, aur 2 interval \([1, 3]\) ka beech (midpoint) hai.
Diya kya hai? Ek lamba sa fraction jo \(x - 2\) ki powers aur \(e^{(x - 2)^2}\) se bana hai.
Kya saabit karna hai? Integral 0 hai.
Rule kaunsa? \(t = x - 2\) rakhenge to interval \([-1, 1]\) ban jayega aur integrand \(t\) mein odd hoga. Phir Property V se seedha 0.
Plan: shift, odd saabit karna, Property V.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(I = \int_{1}^{3} \frac{(x - 2)^3 + 4(x - 2)}{1 + e^{(x - 2)^2}}\,dx\).
Saabit karna: \(I = 0\).
Tareeqa: substitution \(t = x - 2\), phir Property V (\([-a, a]\) par odd function). Jab sab kuch kisi ek cheez ke ird gird likha ho to usi ko naya variable bana dena chahiye.

\(t = x - 2\) rakhein
\[dt = dx,\quad x = 1 \Rightarrow t = -1,\quad x = 3 \Rightarrow t = 1\]
\[I = \int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{t^3 + 4t}{1 + e^{t^2}}\,dt\]
Kyun: is se interval ka beech 0 par aa gaya, aur integrand saaf ho gaya. \(dt = dx\) kyunke sirf 2 ka shift hai.

Odd ya even?
\[g(-t) = \dfrac{-t^3 - 4t}{1 + e^{t^2}} = -g(t)\]
Kyun: upar \(t^3 + 4t\) odd hai (dono odd powers), aur neeche \(1 + e^{t^2}\) even hai (\((-t)^2 = t^2\)). Odd ko even se divide karein to odd hi bachta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(e^{t^2}\) mein \(-t\) rakhne par bhi \(e^{t^2}\) hi aata hai, \(e^{-t^2}\) nahi.

Property V lagayein
\[I = \int_{-1}^{1} g(t)\,dt = 0\]
Kyun: \([-1, 1]\) par odd function ka integral 0 hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 1.5,\ 2.5\ \leftrightarrow\ t = \mp 0.5\]
Kyun: \(x = 2\) ke ird gird aaine wale points par integrand ki values barabar magar ulti hain, to areas cancel. Calculator bhi 0 deta hai.
